newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Copper stages unconvincing rally.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Copper stages unconvincing rally.

text.p: Copper prices attempted to rally on Thursday after heavy losses earlier in the week but investors were not taken-in and prices were on the slide again by the close.
In other commodities palladium prices fell as the Russans started to ship metal again, gold continued to try to stabilise, coffee and soyabeans tumbled on favourable crop weather.
On the London Metal Exchange (LME) copper prices surged up to $65 a tonne higher from Wednesday's $2,230 close as players took some profits by buying back sales made earlier in the week.
But this was seen as just a correction to the week's overall losses and there was no change in the market's fundamental background of slowing summer physical demand and increasing supplies.
"I would have been surprised if there had not been a correction after yesterday (the sharp fall) but the bears are still in the driving-seat," said Angus MacMillan of brokers Billiton Metals.
Near the close the price was already starting to wobble again with earlier gains being halved.

In the precious metals sector palladium, the metal vital to production of auto-exhaust catalysts, dropped as Russia, the world's number one exporter started shipping metal again after a near seven-month break.
The price touched a two-month low of $162 an ounce in Europe, compared to the $240 an ounce level reached in June.
Gold was relatively steady but the action appeared to be similar to that in copper with profits being taken on earlier sales, and the outlook appeared to be for more losses eventually.
"People are short-term bullish and long term bearish for gold,' a dealer said.
It was fixed in London at $319.80 an ounce compared with this week's near 12-year low of $313.60. But several dealers were still expecting a $300 price in the not too distant future.
World coffee prices dropped as stocks started to build in the U.S. and the Department for Agriculture stood by its estimate for a high 28 million bags 1997/98 crop for Brazil.
Also U.S. based Weather Services Corp forecast mild weather seven-days ahead in the Brazil coffee growing areas.
On the London Robusta market September futures fell $54 a tonne to $1,771.
Soyabeans were also hit by good growing weather, this time in the U.S. Midwest, and prices on the Chicago Board of Trade were upto 18 cents a bushel lower at midday.
